title: GOD SPOKE, BUT SHOWED NO FORM

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: You came near and stood at the foot of the mountain while it blazed with fire to the very heavens, with black clouds and deep darkness. Then the Lord spoke to you out of the fire. You heard the sound of words but saw no form; there was only a voice. He declared to you his covenant, the Ten Commandments, which he commanded you to follow and then wrote them on two stone tablets. - Deut 4:11-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses vividly recalls the awesome scene at Horeb (Mount Sinai). The mountain blazed with fire "to the very heavens," wrapped in black clouds and deep darkness, and out of the fire God spoke. The people heard His voice declaring His words, but — and this is crucial — they "saw no form; there was only a voice." God revealed Himself through His word, not through any visible image. This detail becomes the foundation for the warnings against idolatry that follow.

There is profound theology in this. God is Spirit, not a physical form that can be captured in an image (John 4:24). He made Himself known by speaking, revealing His character and will through words rather than a visible shape. This is why the second commandment forbids making images of God — any image would inevitably distort and diminish the God who cannot be contained in created form.

This teaches us how God wants to be known: through His word. The scene at Horeb, terrifying in its majesty, centers on God speaking. He gave His covenant, the Ten Commandments, and wrote them down. God communicates and reveals Himself through His word, and it is there we come to know Him truly.

The wonder of the gospel is that the God who spoke from the fire has spoken even more fully in His Son. Hebrews tells us that in these last days God has spoken to us by His Son (Heb 1:1-2), and John declares that the Word became flesh and dwelt among us (John 1:14). The invisible God has made Himself known in Jesus Christ, "the image of the invisible God" (Col 1:15). We come to know God not through idols of our own making, but through His word, and supremely through Christ. Let us listen for His voice in Scripture and behold His glory in Jesus.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does knowing God reveals Himself through His word shape how you seek Him?
2. Why does God forbid making images of Himself?
3. How does Jesus, the image of the invisible God, make God known to you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You reveal Yourself through Your word, not through images of our making. Help me to know You truly through Scripture, and to behold Your glory in Jesus, the image of the invisible God. Amen.
